summary: A piano keyboard with notes highlighted and labelled, from a chord name ("Dm", "Cmaj7", "Bb/D": the server spells and voices it) or a note list ("D4 F4 A4"); the range fits the notes unless given, and it fills its width.

chord.doc: A chord name: root (C, F#, Bb), quality (m, dim, aug, sus2, sus4, 5, 6, m6, 7, maj7, m7, m7b5, dim7, mMaj7, 7sus4, add9, 9, maj9, m9, 7b9, 7#9, 11, 13, 6/9...) and an optional slash bass (G7/B). Voiced close from the root at `octave`, the slash bass just below it. With notes, it only names the notes (for intervals)

notes.doc: The notes to highlight instead, low to high: "D4 F4 A4" (no octave: rising from octave 4, "A C E" is A4 C5 E5). The chord is identified from them when not given

labels.doc: What the highlighted keys say: "names" (default, spelled for the chord: B♭ not A♯), "intervals" (R, ♭3, 5), "octaves" (D4), "none", or a list of texts, one per note

sub.doc: A second line under the keys, below each highlighted note: "intervals", "names" or a list

range.doc: The keys to draw, ["C3", "B4"]; default: from the C below the lowest note to the B above the highest, two octaves at least

octave.doc: The chord's root octave (4: middle C's octave)

inversion.doc: 1 or 2: the chord's first or second inversion (the lowest notes go up an octave)

height.doc: Key height in dp; the keys share the width

label.doc: Accessibility description; default: the chord's name and the keys

pitfalls: Write the chord or the notes; never colour keys yourself. The server spells the chord from its intervals, so Bbmaj7 reads B♭ D F A, F#7 reads F♯ A♯ C♯ E and E7#9 has an F𝄪
notes with octaves are taken as written (a voicing you choose); without octaves they rise from octave 4

White and black keys are ivory and ebony in every colour theme (they are a piano, not surfaces); the highlight follows the theme. Mono draws white keys as outlines, black keys grey, and highlighted keys solid
Labels need about 7 dp a character per key: on a narrow keyboard they fade out rather than overflow; give fewer keys (range) or a wider box
One canvas, every key a literal rectangle in a box one key wide per white key, scaled to the canvas: about 30 B a key
